title: The data lake and the dashboard connection are removed, so the reporting destinations of three FSD features have no home
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 37, 41 and 44
section: A2.12 Publish the daily reconciliation and freshness report; A2.19 Publish baseline measures; A2.20 Copy the decision log to the lake
description: A2.12 writes the daily data-quality extract to the data lake for a 07:30 dashboard refresh; A2.19 writes the INT-19 extract to the data lake and states a baseline in measure_snapshot with a job at 01:30; A2.20 copies decision log entries to the lake each night at 01:00 with a count and hash check (REC-08). Arch v5 slide 37 removes the data lake and the dashboard connection (INT-19 and INT-20 removed), slide 41 gives measures, snapshots, the steering dashboard and regulatory reports to rwb-reporting, and slide 44 gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting as an Airflow trigger with no data lake and makes decision-log ingest continuous from Kafka in rwb-decision (JOB-13). Three FSD features therefore name a destination and an owner that no longer exist.
evidence: FSD P1 A2.12 integration points 'Power BI, Data lake'; A2.19 integration points 'Power BI, Data lake, ACE database' and AC-ALT-P1-019-02 naming the INT-19 extract; A2.20 integration points 'Data lake' and AC-P1-020-01. Arch v5 slide 37 ('INT-19 and INT-20 removed'), slide 41 (P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard, regulatory reports), slide 44 (JOB-15 owner rwb-reporting, Airflow trigger, no data lake; JOB-13 continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision). Ownership Map: lake_copy_watermark is a P1 legacy table with no target (ASM-A6-tables-13).
proposed: Keep the reconciliation results, the freshness of the 14 data products and the six quality measures as this service's product output, served to rwb-reporting through its snapshot activity and read model; drop the lake copy and the INT-19 extract from this service; publish the measures and any regulatory extract in rwb-reporting; confirm the output channel and the six measure definitions with the data steward before wave 2.

title: The retention rule table and the archive job move to the document service, while the FSD keeps both here
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.17 Apply the retention and archive rule to the data store
description: A2.17 gives this module the retention rule rows (retention_rule) and the monthly archive job (JOB-17) over the recovery tables. Arch v5 slide 16 gives retention to rwb-document, slide 41 gives the document service metadata, custody, signatures and retention, and slide 44 gives JOB-17 to rwb-document as a Temporal Schedule. The Ownership Map records retention_rule as P5 rwb-document and states that P1 drops its retention_rule copy (ASM-A6-tables-10). The product requirement that survives here is the retention class per data product and recovery table, held as data.
evidence: FSD P1 A2.17 description ('JOB-17 runs monthly on the first Sunday'), field catalog on retention_rule, AC-P1-017-01 and AC-ALT-P1-017-01 to -02, AC-EXC-P1-017-03 to -04. Arch v5 slide 16 (P5 OUT: retention), slide 41 (P5 owns retention), slide 44 (JOB-17 owner rwb-document). Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-10.
proposed: This service declares the retention class per data product and recovery table as versioned reference data, refuses a rule that names a read-only ACE view or the decision log, and archives nothing itself; the rule table and the monthly archive run belong to rwb-document. Confirm with Compliance that a class declared here and applied there is acceptable for the PDPA position.

title: Field-level masking rules belong to the access service, while the FSD loads them here
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.15 Set access control per data product for PDPA
description: A2.15 has the data steward load masking rows by role and field ID (masking_rule) in this module, alongside the access rows per role and data product (data_product_access). The Ownership Map gives masking_rule to P4 rwb-access, which owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, the DoA table and the access log (Arch v5 slide 41). The FSD requirement that survives here is role-level read access per data product and the rule that a personal field with no masking row for the role is returned masked.
evidence: FSD P1 A2.15 description and field catalog rows on masking_rule.field_id and masking_rule.unmasked; AC-P1-015-01, AC-ALT-P1-015-01, AC-EXC-P1-015-01 to -02. Arch v5 slide 41 (P4 rwb-access owns masking policy). Ownership Map: masking_rule owner P4.
proposed: This service keeps data_product_access (role, product, read right) and applies the masking policy of rwb-access, cached per the platform pattern; the masking rows themselves are rwb-access's. Confirm the split with Compliance and Security before the first masking test.

title: The case list is split between this service and the case service, while the FSD gives screen and rows to one module
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Ownership Map ruling
section: A2.18 Show the case list with case ID, owner and queue
description: A2.18 gives this module the case list the case owner opens and filters, with the case list rows and the filters on team, queue and product. The Ownership Map keeps the case list operation and screen with P3 rwb-case and gives this service the published daily row set (case_list_row) under the source-default ruling, reading that ruling as the operation and the screen rather than the row table (ASM-A6-tables-2). The reconciliation and the publication hold stay here in either reading.
evidence: FSD P1 A2.18 description and steps 1 to 3 (case owner opens, filters, reads), AC-P1-018-01, AC-ALT-P1-018-01 to -03. Arch v5 slide 41 (P3 owns case, queues, tasks; P1 owns the ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness and reconciliation). Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-2.
proposed: This service builds and publishes one row per case account per business date and holds the publication status; rwb-case serves the case list screen and its filters over those rows; the reconciliation and the hold stay here. Agree the split at the Epic 1 story review.

title: The baseline measure job has two owners, one in the FSD and one in the architecture
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.19; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.19 Publish baseline measures for the recovery portfolio
description: A2.19 runs the measure job at 01:30 inside this module, writes measure_snapshot and sends the extract. Arch v5 slide 44 gives JOB-15 (reporting extract, 01:30) to rwb-reporting as an Airflow trigger with no data lake, and slide 15 gives this service the activity that snapshots a page for measures. The Ownership Map records JOB-15 as P9. The baseline being taken once and frozen is a product requirement that survives; the job that publishes it does not.
evidence: FSD P1 A2.19 description, AC-P1-019-01, AC-ALT-P1-019-01 to -02, AC-EXC-P1-019-02. Arch v5 slide 15 (P1 TMP: snapshot(page) for measures) and slide 44 (JOB-15 owner rwb-reporting). Ownership Map: JOB-15 owner P9.
proposed: This service serves the measure snapshot for a business date whose ACE batches are complete, and rwb-reporting publishes the baseline and freezes it. Confirm that the frozen baseline is not written back to this service.

title: The data-ready and data-late events have two directions and two owners in the source set
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.14; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: A2.14 Stamp each data product with its freshness
description: Arch v5 slide 43 makes rwb-source-data the producer of AceDataReady (row 26) and AceDataLate (row 27) on topic rwb.source-data.events.v1. The Event and Messaging Design v4 marks EV-26 as consumed, with ACE ingestion as the owning module. Under the source precedence rule the architecture catalogue wins, so this service publishes both events; the loser is recorded here.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 rows 26 and 27; slide 15 (P1 OUT: rwb.source-data.events.v1 AceDataReady, AceDataLate at 05:30). Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-26 direction Consumed. Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-flows-4.
proposed: This service publishes both events on its own topic; ACE ingestion stays outside the 19 services and is not a producer on a Recovery topic. Correct the event document at its next version.

title: The Section B views and every Tier 2 feature depend on ACE additions that the ACE team has not accepted
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) OQ-P1-01 and A2.1; BRD Program v4 section 7 (ACE team dependency) and DL43
section: A2.1 Create the recovery tables, extension tables and read-only ACE views; A2.14
description: 14 of the 30 views read 14 new ACE tables and 12 new columns that the ACE team adds under RWB-ACE-001, together with the batch record that freshness depends on. DL43 is open: the scope and dates are not accepted, and the FSD records the dependency as blocking A2.1 Section B, A2.11, A2.14 and A2.18. The batch-status view being a Section B view means freshness itself is behind the dependency.
evidence: FSD P1 OQ-P1-01 and A1.4 preconditions (Section B tables present before the third migration runs); A2.1 view families and AC-EXC-P1-001-06. BRD Program v4 section 7 (ACE team dependency, 14 tables, 12 columns, 80 source fields by 21 November 2026) and section 9 DL43. Arch v5 slide 41 (wave 1).
proposed: Deliver the 16 Section A views, the four extension tables, the dictionary, the reconciliation, the case list and the ledger in wave 1; keep the 14 Section B views, the batch-status freshness source and every Tier 2 feature behind their flags until RWB-ACE-001 lands; confirm the fallback freshness source (CG-9) before system test.

title: The physical dictionary mapping and the system-of-record wording disagree with the frozen view list
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) OQ-P1-03 and OQ-P1-08
section: A2.2; A2.16 Maintain the data catalog entry per data product
description: The physical schema seed maps all 30 view rows to one data product, gives several Section B view fields a text data type whose physical type is integer, and marks two personal view fields as not personal; it also writes systems of record as 'ACE (from ALS via COLLINS)' where the rulings say 'ACE (ingested from X)'. The register's section 8.2 counts 15 and 11 views while the frozen list has 16 and 14. The FSD states that its criteria assume the corrected mapping.
evidence: FSD P1 OQ-P1-03 and OQ-P1-08; AC-P1-001-01 (1,062 of 1,062 table fields and 177 of 177 Section A view fields matched) and AC-ALT-P1-016-02 (304 view fields, 1,062 table fields). BRD Program v4 REQ-RDF-001 wording 'ACE (ingested from the named source)'.
proposed: Correct the seed before the dictionary load: one data product per object family, the physical types the views return, the two personal view fields marked personal, the wording 'ACE (ingested from X)', and the counts 16 and 14.

title: No freshness source is named for the period before the ACE batch record exists
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) OQ-P1-02
section: A2.14 Stamp each data product with its freshness
description: Freshness is read from the batch-status view only, and that view is a Section B view. Before the ACE additions land there is no source of freshness, and the FSD records that the fallback costs Tier 1 views plus the case list without naming a freshness source. The rule that the service never infers freshness from a row count, a file or a view's data date forbids the obvious workaround.
evidence: FSD P1 OQ-P1-02, A2.14 prerequisites ('RWB-ACE-001; v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view'), BR-P1-014-2 and AC-EXC-P1-014-01. BRD Program v4 NFR-014.
proposed: In system test before the ACE additions, read freshness from the batch-status view populated with synthetic batch rows; in any environment without the view, show the data product as not stamped rather than inferring a date. Name the fallback source before the go-live decision.

title: The per-account reconciliation break rows have no store after the quality-exception table leaves the schema
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) OQ-P1-06 and A2.11
section: A2.11 Reconcile the case list to ACE daily; A2.12
description: The reconciliation break rows were written to the removed quality-exception table, and the result table holds only the totals. Two acceptance criteria require the individual account keys to be on a break list for the data steward and, where the key is missing in ACE, for the ACE team. No target table or contract for that list is confirmed.
evidence: FSD P1 OQ-P1-06, A2.11 check table (REC-05 'Zero orphans; every one listed'), AC-ALT-P1-011-01 and AC-ALT-P1-011-03, AC-ALT-P1-012-02. Ownership Map: no P1 table for a break list.
proposed: Publish the break list as part of the reconciliation result and its read operation rather than in a table whose owner is unassigned, and fix the store at the data-model review before system test.

title: Which function writes the appraisal stale flag and age is not set
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) OQ-P1-05; Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-15
section: A2.6 carried rule; A2.1 extension tables
description: The appraisal age rule (stale when more than 365 days old at the business date) moved from the removed appraisal load to the valuation extension row, which holds the stale flag and the age in days. Whether this service or the valuation service writes those two fields is not set, and the extension row is owned here.
evidence: FSD P1 OQ-P1-05 and A2.6 'Carried rule'; FSD P1 field catalog rows valuation_ext.stale_flag (DF-EXT-041) and valuation_ext.age_days (DF-EXT-042). Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-15.
proposed: Hold the rule as data (365 days from the appraisal date to the business date) and write the two fields here until the owning function is assigned; a second writer would break the one-writer rule for an extension row.

title: The classification scheme per data product and the retention periods are open, so the PRD labels are a reading of the field markers
source: BRD Program v4 NFR-047 and DL26; FSD P1 field catalogs
description: Every data product and document type must carry a data classification that sets its handling, but the scheme is open and the retention periods and masking per data product are still to be provided. The only classification evidence in the read sources is the personal-data marker on each field in the FSD field catalogs.
evidence: BRD Program v4 NFR-047 ('classification scheme to be applied', open), NFR-028, NFR-031 and DL26. FSD P1 field catalogs (personal data column) and A2.15.
proposed: Apply the four-label scheme from the field markers now: personal fields and the party and contact extension rows as personal data, balances and amounts as sensitive financial data, case, legal, collateral and metadata as confidential, and no data product as public. Replace with the approved scheme when DL26 closes.

title: Two module specifications define the ledger tables and the ownership map leaves both here
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling ASM-A6-tables-1; FSD P1 A2.11 prerequisites
description: The case module specification defines the interaction table for its own timeline operation and the integration module specification defines the ledger intake rule table, while the source-default ruling puts the interaction ledger with this service, keeps the case timeline operation in the case service, and has integration read the ledger through this service's contract. The Epic 1 requirements place ledger read and write with the case owner role.
evidence: Ownership Map: interaction and efs_ledger_outcome owner P1, ruling ASM-A6-tables-1. FSD P1 A2.11 and A2.18 read case and contact data through the case contract. BRD Epic 1 v4 REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-008 and RWB-E1-066 to RWB-E1-068.
proposed: This service owns the ledger tables and the write path; rwb-case serves the case timeline over this service's contract; rwb-integration writes intake outcomes through the same contract. One writer per ledger.

title: Four tables carry a name, an owner and a purpose but no field list in the read sources
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.2 and A2.16; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15; Ownership Map
description: The data contract table, the two dated Stage 2 data-product copies for treatments and guarantee claims, and the ledger intake rule table are each named and owned, with a stated purpose and ruling, but no source in the read set lists their fields, types or keys. The field catalogues in the functional specification cover the four extension tables, the data product catalog, the access rows, the masking rows, the retention rows, the dictionary and the case list rows only.
evidence: Ownership Map tables data_contract, dp_treatment, dp_guarantee_claim and efs_ledger_outcome (owner P1, rulings ASM-A6-tables-14 and ASM-A6-tables-1). FSD P1 field catalogs A2.1, A2.2, A2.15, A2.16, A2.17, A2.18. Arch v5 slide 15 (P1 schema: ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness, reconciliation).
proposed: Carry the field lists as placeholders in this version and fix them at the technical specification review before wave 2; do not spend the Stage 2 copies before the contracts, plans and treatments events exist.

title: The bank scheduler contract is a recommendation in the architecture, not an agreed interface
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 and its notes; FSD P1 OQ-P1-02
description: The business-date ready call, its idempotency on the date, the status values and the sensor that waits for the daily case run are presented as a recommendation to discuss, and four points remain open: who owns the scheduler DAGs, when the current scheduler is replaced, where the scheduler runs, and whether the ACE ingestion chain is still on the current scheduler at go-live. The functional specification assumes a poll of the ACE batch record instead.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 32 ('Interface contract: scheduler to Recovery', 'To agree (for discussion)') and its notes naming the poll fallback; slide 31 notes (the last ingestion task calls the service, which checks freshness and publishes the ready event). FSD P1 A2.14 steps and OQ-P1-02.
owner_role: Solution architect with the bank platform team
proposed: Implement both paths: the ready and status operations for the scheduler, and the poll of the ACE batch record as the fallback. Confirm which is live at go-live before the integration test.

title: The job monitor and data-quality screens are first-in here and owned by reporting in the architecture
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
description: The functional specification lists the interface and job monitor and the data quality screens with this module, first in Epic 2 and at full scope in Epic 8. The architecture gives the steering dashboard and the reporting surfaces to rwb-reporting, and the edge serves screens through a composite route that joins several services. No source states which service owns the screen shell, its states or its route.
evidence: FSD P1 Screens table (SCR-44 Interface and job monitor; SCR-45 Data quality). Arch v5 slide 41 (P9 owns the steering dashboard and reporting), slide 20 and slide 48 (gateway-bff composite route for staff screens). Ownership Map: the job and data-quality operations are P1's.
proposed: This service serves the job, freshness, reconciliation and dictionary operations; the composite route is the edge's and the dashboard shell is reporting's. Fix the screen owner before Epic 2 acceptance.

title: No approval status is recorded for the business requirements in this run
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 and Epic 1 v4 (no governance or sign-off table); run rules (no human approval step)
description: The business requirements carry no governance table, approval record or signature block in the converted text, so the precondition that the upstream baseline is approved with a product owner decision cannot be verified. The run rules remove human approval stops, so the work continues and the status is Draft.
evidence: BRD Program v4 document control table (document, version, date, prepared by, covers, structure, change) with no status, owner decision or sign-off; BRD Epic 1 v4 document control and section 6 (acceptance by business testers) with no approval record.
proposed: Carry the PRD as Draft with an empty approval table; record the product owner and FDA decisions when they are taken, without changing the requirement substance.
